home.headline: Your home: keys around July 2027.
assumptions: Assumed: first-time buyer; a 30-year mortgage with a €35,000 deposit (10%); a €350,000 home, as given; not a new build, so no Help to Buy and standard rates (a BER C where a lender prices by BER); stamp duty of €3,500 (1%) and €3,000 for legal fees and a survey (an estimate); costs compared over 30 years for every lender, at each lender’s stated follow-on rate after the fixed period.

conditions: 1% or 2% at drawdown, by product (CCPC’s words; avantmoney.ie refused automated reads).
pathways.line: With Avant Money: keys around July 2027; Up to 30 year fixed >80% <=90% at 3.8% (€1,467.77 a month), €3,150 cashback at drawdown; the lowest cost over 30 years (incentives from CCPC’s tables, not confirmed on the lender’s site).

mortgage.name: Capped Variable Rate Mortgage - Capped at 4.40% (APRC 4.50%)* for first 3 years.

pathways.line: With Credit Union Mortgages: keys around July 2027; Capped Variable Rate Mortgage - Capped at 4.40% (APRC 4.50%)* for first 3 years. at 3.85% (€1,476.75 a month), no cashback or bonus; about €6,383 more over 30 years than the lowest.

pathways.drivers: MortgageSaver bonus €1,340 after DIRT, €6,300 cashback at drawdown, €3,150 more after 5 years
conditions: 2% within 45 days of drawdown; 1% more after 5 years if every repayment is made in full and on time. Fixed rates only, not High Value Mortgage rates.

MortgageSaver: €2,000 less DIRT, paid into the account within 5 working days of a Bank of Ireland first-time-buyer mortgage being drawn down in full: €200 to €2,500 a month by direct debit for 6 months in a row, €5,000 or more saved and still held at drawdown, within 30 months of opening. One bonus per mortgage; one account per person; can be held alongside SuperSaver.
The bonus is paid after drawdown, so it lowers the cost rather than the deposit needed: the keys date is the same.
pathways.line: With Bank of Ireland: keys around July 2027; 5 Year Fixed BER C at 4% (€1,503.86 a month), MortgageSaver bonus €1,340 after DIRT, €6,300 cashback at drawdown, €3,150 more after 5 years; about €12,462 more over 30 years than the lowest.

€45,197 in all at November 2027: €45,197 towards the first home (no debts given).
The split this plan uses: €35,000 in MoCo EasySaver; €675 a month in Bank of Ireland SuperSaver Account; €100 a month in EBS d.a.c Family Savings Account (Fixed); €25 a month in AIB Online Saver.
Everything stays in instant access: a fixed term would add only €70.35 by November 2027.
Each extra €100 a month adds about €1,213.06 by November 2027.

Help to Buy: depends, up to €35,000 on €350,000: the lesser of 10% of a new build’s price (up to €500,000), €35,000 (applications from 2026-10-07) and the Income Tax and DIRT paid over the last four years, for homes bought or built by 2029-12-31. The refund is also limited to the Income Tax and DIRT paid over the last four tax years, which was not given. Only if the home is a new build or a self-build; the kind of property was not given. Source: Revenue, https://www.revenue.ie/en/property/help-to-buy-incentive/how-much-can-you-claim.aspx, checked 2026-11-09; saoi_first_home works it out for a price.
To sharpen this, the customer could say: (1) Roughly what price, and is it a new build? Help to Buy and green rates apply to new builds; the price sets the keys date.
This plan can be opened in the Saoi app: https://app.saoi.ie/#/plan/99aOrER3w7s12Jy0DFTWEw (held for 24 hours, then deleted unless opened).
These are options with their figures, for the inputs given; the customer decides.

moneyFound.basis: A year’s figures, after DIRT at 33%: idle cash against the best confirmed instant-access rate (only where its current rate was given), debt interest not paid in the next twelve months less what the same money would earn, and a mortgage switch’s lower repayment. Bonuses, cashback and rates resting on CCPC’s one figure are not counted. In a plan, debt figures are the plan’s own net positions, spread over its 12 months.

products.why: €35,000 in MoCo EasySaver: the most known interest after DIRT for this part of the money.
checks: Protected by the Austrian deposit guarantee (Einlagensicherung AUSTRIA) up to €100,000, not the Irish scheme.
Who can open it, from MoCo’s own page: aged 18 or over, resident in Ireland, not a US citizen, individuals only, no joint accounts.
2.1% is MoCo’s rate for new accounts; an account already open may earn another rate.

depositGuarantee.note: MoCo is a trading name of BAWAG P.S.K. (Irish branch); the €100,000 is shared across BAWAG’s brands.

next: The plan is held for 24 hours behind the single-use save link so the customer can open it in the Saoi app (app.saoi.ie), then deleted unless opened; nothing else is stored. Offer the link. In the app the plan opens as a card, and Saoirse, Saoi’s assistant, knows it and can talk it through; signing in with an email address keeps it across devices, including the installed app. Alerts when a chosen product’s rate changes and reminders as the goal date nears are coming, not built yet. To compare options (a debt kept or cleared, another monthly amount or date), pass them as `alternatives` in one saoi_build_plan call; call it again only when the customer changes their situation in a later message.
